key_insight: Apollo is a room-temperature neuromorphic processor that uses quantum-derived randomness in p-qubits to emulate key behaviors of transverse-field quantum annealing without cryogenics.
engineering_relevance: The architecture offers an industrially scalable path for solving dense Ising/QUBO optimization problems with lower embedding overhead and analog power around 0.5 W.
method: 10000-node p-qubit neuromorphic processor in 16 nm mixed-signal CMOS
Integrated quantum entropy units inject true randomness into bistable stochastic units
High-connectivity Hyperion 256 topology supports dense problem embedding
evidence_signal: Across 300 spin-glass disorder realizations, Apollo achieved lower ground-state energies than reported cryogenic annealing hardware, and a 350 nm release candidate validated p-qubit dynamics and thermodynamic sampling.
watch_item: The approach still depends on analog stochastic hardware behavior, so scaling, calibration stability, and reproducibility across large deployments may be challenging.
paper_title: Quantum-Driven Neuromorphic Computing for Million-Qubit-Scale Workloads
